title: Activation readiness schematic and decision journal
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, working schematic plus a decision journal for feature activation windows. It is intended for product-ops, release engineers, SRE oncall, and feature owners. Use it as the single source for: (1) a concise readiness checklist, (2) KPI thresholds and measurement definitions, (3) traffic scenario probes and expected operator decisions, and (4) a rolling log of decisions and rationale taken during the pre-launch and first 72 hours post-activation.

Quick summary (one line):
Activation will proceed in 3 phases (pilot -> measured ramp -> full release). The activation decision boundary is a combined rule: SLO pass AND no critical errors AND capacity margin >= 18% for two consecutive 10-minute windows. If any rule fails, follow the fallback ladder.

Audience and owners:
- Primary owner: Alyssa Chen (product-ops)
- Release engineer: Ravi Patel
- SRE escalation: Ethan Brooks
- Feature PM: Mariana López
- UX/Product analyst: (TBD)

Timing and phases (dates are placeholders - update from release calendar):
- Pilot (canary cohort, 1% traffic): 2026-02-18 07:00 -> 2026-02-18 13:00 (6h probe)
- Measured ramp (10% -> 50% over 48h): 2026-02-19 -> 2026-02-21
- Full release (100%): target 2026-02-22 03:00

KPI definitions and concrete thresholds (operators must check these before and during each phase):
- User-visible latency P95 (generation end-to-end): threshold A = 350ms (pilot), threshold B = 420ms (ramp), threshold C = 600ms (full).
- Token-cost per request (observed mean): baseline_ref = historical window (7d) for same route. Acceptable delta: <= +15% during ramp.
- Error rate (5xx from runtime + application errors): must be <= 0.4% sustained over 10m for pilot. If >0.8% immediate abort.
- Throughput saturation (% GPUs util): keep <78% on serving pools for pilot; <88% for ramp; <95% for full.
- KV cache hit ratio: must not regress >5 percentage points vs baseline.
- Quality regression signal (evaluation set scoring): automated evaluation must show no more than 2% drop on core prompt set (see linked eval job: confluence:PRODOPS-3124).

Decision heuristic (machine-readable summary):
ACTIVATE_PHASE(next_phase) when:
  (latency_p95 <= threshold(next_phase)) AND
  (error_rate_10m <= threshold_err(next_phase)) AND
  (gpu_margin >= margin(next_phase)) AND
  (quality_drop <= 2%)
Else: HOLD or ROLLBACK according to severity.

Escalation ladder (quick):
- Tier 0: on-call SRE receives alert -> check serving runtime dashboards and tail traces (console -> traces).
- Tier 1: if error rate >0.8% or latency P95 > 2x threshold -> abort ramp and instantly shift traffic to previous stable model variant.
- Tier 2: repeated anomalies across regions or model variants -> engage Engineering triage (pager).

Contingency/fallback options (ordered):
1) Automated fallback to smaller model variant (same family, lower latency) - immediate, transparent to users for 2xx fallthrough.
2) Traffic re-routing to Dedicated capacity pool in US-WEST (if private capacity reserved).
3) Throttle non-critical routes and background batch jobs (cost control).
4) Full rollback to previous model and configuration.

Traffic scenario probes (what to run during pilot window):
- Baseline probe: replay 5000 synthetic requests representative of 10k DAU at 1% sample. Observe 30m moving averages.
- Spike probe: 3 x 30s bursts at 5x baseline QPS to measure latency tail behavior and runtime backpressure.
- Prefix-heavy probe: 2k long-context requests (avg seq_len 1024) to stress KV cache and memory kernels.
- Edge-case probe: 1k adversarial prompts from internal eval set to surface quality regressions.

Checklist - pre-pilot (must be green before pilot starts):
- [ ] Config pin for canary cohort implemented and validated in Console (owner: Release eng)
- [ ] Autoscaling policy validated for spike probe (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Canary metrics dashboard snapshot saved (owner: Product-ops)
- [ ] E2E smoke tests run from two geographic regions (EU, US) and pass (owner: QA)
- [ ] KMS keys and audit logging verified for the model artifact (owner: Security)
- [ ] Rollback playbook accessible from Console (owner: Product-ops)
- [ ] Customer comms draft in case of incident (owner: PM)

Checklist - during pilot (live items):
- Period: continuous 10m windows; primary operator to tick off every window.
- [ ] Confirm latency_p95 and error_rate in last 10m (owner: operator)
- [ ] Inspect any error trace with >5 occurrences (owner: Release eng)
- [ ] Confirm cost delta within allowed bounds (owner: Finance ops)
- [ ] Run quick quality sampling (10 prompts) for human check if automated eval flags drop (owner: PM / UX researcher)
- [ ] If any threshold breached, execute fallback step 1 and escalate (owner: SRE)

Checklist - ramp to 50%:
- [ ] Validate regional parity across top 3 regions (owner: Release eng)
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler behavior under triaged spikes (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Confirm telemetry retention for 72h (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Customer support readiness line-up completed (owner: CS lead)

Operational notes and practical heuristics (notes to self / running tips):
- "If token cost jumps but latency stable": suspect batching or kernel change. Check batch size histogram and kernel selection logs in infra logs.
- "If KV cache hit drops sharply": check model rollout for changed tokenizer offset or prefix handling; compare prefix distributions to baseline.
- When aborting, keep a copy of 5-minute trace window for postmortem (don't discard).

Metrics collection endpoints and quick queries (examples):
- latency P95: metrics namespace "redwood.requests.latency_p95" with tag route:<route>,model:<model>
- error rate: "redwood.requests.errors.count" / "redwood.requests.total.count" windowed
- gpu util margin: derived -> 1 - (gpu_util_observed / gpu_util_capacity)
- sample PromQL snip (console friendly): rate(redwood_requests_errors_total[10m]) / rate(redwood_requests_total[10m]) > 0.008 -> alert

Open questions and unresolved items (action items):
- Who will own the UX sampling checklist during overnight windows? (Assigned: Mariana to confirm by 2026-02-07)
- Confirm Dedicated pool routing permissions for customer A (legal/contract review pending) -> blocker for fallback 2.
- Need a short script to automate the 3x spike probe; can we reuse infra/loadtest library? (Ravi to prototype)

Decision journal (rolling, populate during run):
- 2026-02-18 07:20: Pilot started. Initial 30m shows latency_p95 320ms, error_rate 0.12%. Proceeding. (A.C.)
- 2026-02-18 08:05: Observed 2x spike at 07:58 for 45s with p95 -> 620ms but error_rate stayed low. Took no action; flagged for longer observation. (E.B.)
- 2026-02-18 09:12: KV cache hit ratio dropped 7pp vs baseline after a tokenizer tweak; executed fallback to smaller model variant at 09:20. Latency returned to expected. Rollback reason: cache regress. (R.P.)

Postmortem anchors (if rollback or incident):
- Capture: dashboard snapshot, full trace export, container events, autoscaler logs, model artifact hash, commit SHAs, and canary cohort ids.
- Postmortem sections required: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, follow-up owners, SLA impact calculation, learning items.

Appendix: short runbook snippets (copy into Console runbooks):
- Abort ramp command (one-liner): console api traffic.shift --route <route> --to-model <model-id> --cohort 0
- Snapshot dashboards: console dashboards.snapshot --id <dash-id> --label "pilot-snap-<timestamp>"
- Quick rollback: infra release rollback --artifact <artifact-hash> --reason "canary-cache-regress"

Notes to readers: This file is intended to be the working journal during the activation window. Keep edits minimal during live ops; instead add to the Decision journal at the bottom. After closure of the activity, distill the decisions into the canonical postmortem doc and link into confluence:PRODOPS-3124.

---
End of working schematic.
